topics.topic: Quranic Exegesis: Study, recitation, and lessons from Suratul Mulk (Quran 67:1-15)
learningObjectives: Recite verses 1-15 of Suratul Mulk adhering to Tajweed rules of elongation and ghunnah
Translate verses highlighting the perfection of divine cosmic creation and the test of deeds
Explain the purpose of human life and death as a divine trial for righteous conduct

topics.topic: Quranic Exegesis: Suratul Mulk (Quran 67:16-30) on accountability and the Hereafter
learningObjectives: Recite verses 16-30 with proper Arabic phonetic pronunciation and intonation
Analyze warnings regarding divine punishment, the questioning of disbelievers in Hell, and God’s knowledge of secrets
Derive lessons on gratitude for divine gifts of hearing, sight, and understanding

topics.topic: Hadith Collections and Canonical Compilers: The Sihahus-Sittah (Six Authentic Books)
learningObjectives: List the authors of the six sound Hadith collections (Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawood, Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah)
Examine the rigorous biographical and textual verification methodology adopted by Imam al-Bukhari
Differentiate between Sahih (sound), Hasan (good), Da'if (weak), and Mawdu' (fabricated) Hadiths

topics.topic: Hadith on Good Character: Hadith 13 (Brotherhood) and Hadith 15 (Guarding the Tongue)
learningObjectives: Recite, translate, and explain Hadith 13: 'None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself'
Recite and explain Hadith 15: 'Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent'
Apply these teachings to conflict reduction, peer empathy, and social media etiquette

topics.topic: Shari'ah (Islamic Jurisprudence): Sources of Islamic Law (Quran, Sunnah, Ijma, Qiyas)
learningObjectives: Define Shari'ah as the divine pathway and constitutional code governing all facets of Muslim life
Explain the two primary immutable sources: the Holy Quran and the authentic Sunnah
Examine secondary derived sources: Ijma (consensus of scholars) and Qiyas (analogical deduction)

topics.topic: Islamic Family Law: Marriage (Nikah) conditions, rights of spouses, and Mahr
learningObjectives: State essential pillars of valid Nikah (mutual consent, Wali/guardian approval, two just witnesses, Mahr)
Explain the theological purpose of marriage: companionship, chastity, and righteous lineage
Outline reciprocal rights and obligations of husband and wife in an Islamic household

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Islamic Law Colloquium
learningObjectives: Assess pupil comprehension of Suratul Mulk, Hadith criticism, and Shari'ah jurisprudence
Conduct a debate on 'Analogical Deduction (Qiyas) in Resolving Modern Technological Dilemmas'
Offer remedial intervention on the categorization of Hadith authenticity

topics.topic: Islamic Family Law: Dissolution of Marriage (Talaq, Khul', and Iddah periods)
learningObjectives: Examine the stages of marital reconciliation prior to divorce in the Quran (4:35)
Distinguish between Talaq (repudiation by husband) and Khul' (redemption initiated by wife)
Explain the theological and biological wisdom behind the Iddah (waiting period) of divorce and widowhood

topics.topic: History of the Rightly Guided Caliphs: Caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
learningObjectives: Trace the appointment of Abu Bakr at Saqifah and his resolute stand against the apostasy wars (Riddah)
Analyze the military administrative genius of Umar: establishment of Diwan, judicial system, and expansion
Highlight personal virtues of Umar: simplicity, accountability, and justice for all citizens

topics.topic: History of the Rightly Guided Caliphs: Caliphate of Uthman and Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
learningObjectives: Analyze the achievements of Uthman: naval fleet establishment and compiling the standardized Mushaf
Examine the civil strife (Fitnah) resulting in the tragic assassination of Uthman
Trace the Caliphate of Ali, his wisdom, scholarly depth, and challenges at the Battles of the Camel and Siffin

topics.topic: Economic System of Islam: Prohibition of Riba (Usury), Gharar (Excessive Risk), and Bribery
learningObjectives: Define Riba (interest/usury) and explain stern Quranic condemnations against exploitative financial lending
Explain Gharar and its application to fraudulent contractual agreements and gambling
Examine the prophetic condemnation of the giver and receiver of bribes (Rishwah) in public service

topics.topic: Comprehensive SSS 2 IRS Termly Revision & WASSCE Past Paper Analysis
learningObjectives: Consolidate learning across Quranic exegesis, Hadith, Shari'ah family law, and Caliphate history
Execute timed essay responses simulating WASSCE IRS Paper 2 questions
Audit student understanding of Arabic terminology and jurisprudential reasoning
Administer official SSS 2 end-of-term IRS examination
Score scripts in strict accordance with WAEC marking guidelines
Record and publish moderated terminal continuous assessment marks
